title: AI-classified XPCS links local relaxation episodes with bulk stress changes in a colloidal glass
summary: In rheo-XPCS measurements of a sheared silica-nanoparticle glass, an unsupervised convolutional autoencoder and K-means clustering grouped two-time correlation patterns by relative relaxation rate. Changes in the frequencies of slow-dynamics classes tracked non-monotonic shear-stress relaxation, while some later local slow-dynamics episodes appeared without a corresponding change in the bulk stress signal. This is a measured microscopic-to-macroscopic relationship in the study’s model colloidal system.
ai_technology: AI-NERD: convolutional autoencoder for XPCS correlation images with K-means clustering in the learned latent space
organization: Argonne National Laboratory; University of Chicago; University of Illinois Chicago

evidence.tested: In rheo-XPCS measurements of a sheared silica-nanoparticle glass, an unsupervised convolutional autoencoder and K-means clustering grouped two-time correlation patterns by relative relaxation rate.
evidence.unknown: The findings come from rheo-XPCS of a model concentrated silica-nanoparticle suspension under the reported shear/relaxation protocol. Cluster labels encode relative relaxation rates and latent-space distances are not quantitative physical measures. The authors describe the stress/dynamics relationship qualitatively and say further work is needed to extract quantitative physical information. A publisher correction dated 2024-09-09 corrected corresponding-author information; it did not report a change to the results.
evidence.ai_role: The unsupervised neural autoencoder compressed experimental two-time X-ray photon correlation functions into a latent representation, then K-means grouped frames by dynamical similarity. Class-transition frequencies over experimental time let researchers compare local relaxation patterns with simultaneous rheometer stress measurements, revealing where local slow dynamics coincided with stress minima and where they did not.
